messages.content:
For breakfast I had a 12 ounce iced coffee and a banana.

For lunch I had a quesadilla

Breakfast four ounces of asparagus, two eggs, one piece of gluten free bread.

function.name: log_food
function.description: Logs a food item with details about the portion size and the meal it is associated with. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

food_name.description: The name of the food to log.

portion_amount.description: The amount of the food item that was consumed, in specified units. This is a float type value.

portion_unit.description: The unit of measure for the portion amount. Choose a unit such as 'grams', 'ounces', 'pieces', 'cups', or 'tablespoons'.

meal_name.description: The name of the meal with which the food item is associated. Options include 'breakfast', 'lunch', 'dinner', or 'snack'.

They didn't specify portion amounts for banana, quesadilla. We need to log each item with portion amount and unit. For banana, typical portion maybe 1 banana (piece). For quesadilla, we need portion amount; maybe 1 quesadilla (piece). But we can ask clarifying question. But the instruction: "When you do not know the portion size, ask the user for clarification." So we should ask for portion sizes for banana and quesadilla. Also for the iced coffee, portion unit is ounces, amount 12. For asparagus, 4 oz. Eggs: 2 pieces. Bread: 1 piece. So we can log those. Then ask for banana portion and quesadilla portion. Also ask if they want to log banana as 1 piece. But we can ask for portion amount and unit. Let's ask clarifying question: "How many bananas did you eat? And how many quesadillas?" Also ask for portion unit for banana (pieces) and quesadilla (pieces). Then we can log.
